subtopics.name: Exactly solvable lattice models
subtopics.scope: Classical two-dimensional and quantum one-dimensional lattice models (vertex, Potts, dimer, hard-hexagon, spin chains) whose free energies, order parameters, or spectra can be obtained in closed form.

subtopics.name: Critical phenomena and renormalization group
subtopics.scope: Equilibrium continuous phase transitions in O(N), Potts, and related models in general dimension, focusing on universality classes, critical exponents, crossover behavior, and multicritical points.

subtopics.name: Two-dimensional criticality and conformal invariance
subtopics.scope: Critical and quasi-long-range-ordered two-dimensional systems analyzed through conformal symmetry, including boundary critical behavior, Kosterlitz-Thouless transitions, and loop-model or SLE descriptions of critical curves.

subtopics.name: Mean-field spin glasses and replica symmetry breaking
subtopics.scope: Ising, p-spin, spherical, and Potts spin-glass models with fully connected or sparse random couplings, their thermodynamics, ergodicity breaking, and energy-landscape complexity.

subtopics.name: Random magnets and quenched disorder
subtopics.scope: Effects of quenched randomness in couplings, fields, or site occupation on finite-dimensional phase transitions, including random-field and diluted magnets, rare-region effects, and infinite-randomness critical points.

subtopics.name: Percolation and geometric phase transitions
subtopics.scope: Connectivity transitions of random clusters on lattices, continua, and random graphs, including thresholds, cluster-size statistics, fractal dimensions, and variants such as bootstrap, continuum, and explosive percolation.

subtopics.name: Statistical mechanics of neural networks and learning
subtopics.scope: Typical-case analysis of associative memories and of learning in perceptrons, committee machines, and wide or deep networks, focusing on storage capacity, generalization curves, and high-dimensional training dynamics.

subtopics.name: Random constraint satisfaction and high-dimensional inference
subtopics.scope: Phase transitions in random combinatorial optimization and planted inference problems such as satisfiability, coloring, matching, community detection, and compressed sensing.

subtopics.name: Spectra of random matrices and operators
subtopics.scope: Eigenvalue densities, spacing statistics, extreme eigenvalues, and eigenvector properties of random matrix ensembles, including sparse, structured, and non-Hermitian ones.

subtopics.name: Anderson and many-body localization
subtopics.scope: Localization of waves and quantum particles by disorder or quasiperiodicity, from single-particle mobility edges and multifractal critical states to interacting many-body localization.

subtopics.name: Quantum quenches and isolated-system thermalization
subtopics.scope: Nonequilibrium dynamics of isolated quantum many-body systems after quenches, covering thermalization, generalized Gibbs ensembles, entanglement growth, and generalized hydrodynamics of integrable chains.

subtopics.name: Driven lattice gases and nonequilibrium transport
subtopics.scope: Boundary-driven and bulk-driven stochastic particle and energy transport models, such as exclusion and zero-range processes and oscillator chains, focusing on steady states, currents, phase diagrams, and anomalous conduction.

subtopics.name: KPZ interface growth and directed polymers
subtopics.scope: Stochastic interface growth and directed polymers in random media, including scaling exponents, height and free-energy distributions, and exact solutions in the Kardar-Parisi-Zhang universality class.

subtopics.name: Random walks, first passage, and extremes
subtopics.scope: Statistics of random walks, Brownian motion, and related stochastic processes, including first-passage and survival probabilities, extreme-value and record statistics, path functionals, and stochastic resetting.

subtopics.name: Stochastic thermodynamics and fluctuation relations
subtopics.scope: Thermodynamics of small systems driven out of equilibrium, including entropy production, work and heat fluctuations, uncertainty relations, efficiency of microscopic engines, and the thermodynamics of information.

subtopics.name: Active matter and self-propelled particles
subtopics.scope: Statistical mechanics of particles that consume energy to self-propel, covering run-and-tumble and active Brownian dynamics, motility-induced phase separation, flocking, and active pressure and boundary accumulation.

subtopics.name: Coarsening, aging, and phase-ordering kinetics
subtopics.scope: Relaxation of systems quenched into ordered or critical phases, including domain-growth laws, dynamical scaling, autocorrelation exponents, aging, and kinetic Ising and voter dynamics.

subtopics.name: Absorbing-state transitions and reaction-diffusion kinetics
subtopics.scope: Nonequilibrium phase transitions into absorbing states and the kinetics of diffusion-limited reactions, including directed percolation, contact and epidemic processes, branching-annihilating walks, and sandpile models of self-organized criticality.

subtopics.name: Glasses, jamming, and amorphous solids
subtopics.scope: Structural glass formation and jamming of disordered packings, including mean-field theories in infinite dimensions, mode-coupling dynamics, random first-order transitions, kinetically constrained models, and marginal stability.

subtopics.name: Classical fluids and kinetic theory
subtopics.scope: Equilibrium and transport properties of classical fluids and hard-core gases, including virial coefficients, integral-equation and density-functional theories, exactly solvable one-dimensional fluids, and Boltzmann-equation kinetics of molecular and granular gases.

subtopics.name: Polymers, self-avoiding walks, and lattice paths
subtopics.scope: Statistics of polymer chains and lattice path ensembles, including self-avoiding walks, adsorption and collapse transitions, stretched polymers, vesicles, and enumeration of lattice animals.

subtopics.name: Long-range interactions and synchronization
subtopics.scope: Systems with long-range or all-to-all couplings, including Hamiltonian mean-field and self-gravitating models, ensemble inequivalence, quasi-stationary states, and Kuramoto-type synchronization of coupled oscillators.

techniques.name: Transfer matrices and duality transformations
techniques.scope: Writing partition functions as traces of transfer-matrix powers and using Kramers-Wannier-type dualities to obtain free energies, correlation lengths, and exact critical points.

techniques.name: Coordinate and algebraic Bethe ansatz
techniques.scope: Diagonalizing integrable Hamiltonians and transfer matrices via Bethe equations, then extracting ground-state energies, excitation spectra, and thermodynamic-Bethe-ansatz thermodynamics in the thermodynamic limit.

techniques.name: Free-fermion, Pfaffian, and dimer mappings
techniques.scope: Mapping spin chains, planar Ising models, or dimer coverings onto quadratic fermion problems (Jordan-Wigner, Kasteleyn Pfaffians) to compute spectra, correlations, and entanglement exactly.

techniques.name: Replica method with symmetry breaking
techniques.scope: Averaging the logarithm of disordered partition functions via replicas and evaluating the saddle point under replica-symmetric or Parisi-type ansatze to obtain free energies, thresholds, and stability lines.

techniques.name: Cavity method and message passing
techniques.scope: Solving models on sparse random graphs or dense factor graphs through cavity recursions, belief propagation, state evolution, and population dynamics to obtain thresholds and typical-case observables.

techniques.name: Perturbative field-theoretic renormalization group
techniques.scope: Computing beta functions, fixed points, and critical exponents to fixed order in epsilon or 1/N expansions from Landau-Ginzburg-Wilson and related continuum actions.

techniques.name: Real-space and strong-disorder renormalization
techniques.scope: Decimation, Migdal-Kadanoff, and strong-disorder renormalization schemes that produce recursion relations whose fixed points give exact or approximate critical couplings and exponents.

techniques.name: Conformal field theory and Coulomb gas
techniques.scope: Using conformal and modular invariance and Coulomb-gas mappings to determine scaling dimensions, finite-size amplitudes, boundary exponents, and critical correlation functions in two dimensions.

techniques.name: Saddle-point and large-N asymptotics
techniques.scope: Evaluating partition functions, generating functions, and integrals asymptotically via Laplace and steepest-descent methods in spherical, O(N)-vector, mean-field, and other large-parameter limits.

techniques.name: Response-field path integrals and dynamical mean-field theory
techniques.scope: Martin-Siggia-Rose-Janssen-De Dominicis and Doi-Peliti functional integrals, and the dynamical mean-field equations they yield, for Langevin and stochastic reaction dynamics of interacting or disordered systems.

techniques.name: Exact solution of master equations
techniques.scope: Solving master, Fokker-Planck, and backward Kolmogorov equations exactly via generating functions, eigenfunction expansions, and image methods to obtain stationary states and time-dependent distributions.

techniques.name: Renewal theory and Laplace-transform methods
techniques.scope: Using renewal equations, Laplace transforms, and Sparre Andersen or Pollaczek-Spitzer formulas to obtain first-passage, survival, record, and resetting statistics of stochastic processes.

techniques.name: Large deviations and tilted generators
techniques.scope: Computing rate functions and scaled cumulant generating functions of empirical and time-integrated observables via tilted generators, Gartner-Ellis and contraction principles, and macroscopic fluctuation theory.

techniques.name: Matrix product ansatz for steady states
techniques.scope: Representing nonequilibrium steady states of stochastic lattice models as products of matrices obeying quadratic algebras to compute currents, density profiles, correlations, and phase diagrams.

techniques.name: Resolvent and free-probability methods
techniques.scope: Determining spectral densities, edges, and extreme eigenvalues of random matrices and operators via Stieltjes transforms, self-consistent resolvent equations, R- and S-transforms, and log-gas energy minimization.

techniques.name: Cluster, virial, and series expansions
techniques.scope: Mayer cluster, virial, high- and low-temperature, and exact-enumeration series expansions combined with ratio or Pade analysis to obtain thermodynamic coefficients, thresholds, and critical exponents.
